**The Imjin War (1592–1598)** | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Full name** | Imjin War (임진왜란) – “Imjin” refers to the year 1592 in the sex‑celestial stem‑branch calendar. | | **Belligerents** | • **Japan** – led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, seeking to conquer Korea and expand influence into China.
• **Joseon Korea** – a tributary state of Ming China, defended by its own forces and later aided by Ming troops.
• **Ming China** – sent a large expeditionary force to support Joseon after the Japanese invasion. | | **Timeline** | • **April 1592** – Japanese forces land on the Korean coast (Busan).
• **Late 1592** – Japanese armies advance north, capturing Seoul and the capital city of Gyeongju.
• **Early 1593** – Ming forces arrive; the Battle of Hansan Island (June 1592) and the Battle of Myeongnyang (1597) are key naval victories for the Koreans/Ming.
• **1597–1598** – Japanese forces retreat; the war ends with the Treaty of Gyeongju (1598). | | **Key Battles** | • **Battle of Hansan Island** – Admiral Yi Sun-sin’s torpedo‑driven “geobukseon” (turtle ships) decimate Japanese navy.
• **Battle of Myeongnyang** – Yi Sun-sin defeats a larger Japanese fleet with only 13 ships.
• **Battle of Noryang** – final naval engagement; Yi Sun-sin dies in the battle. | | **Major Outcomes** | • **Military** – Japan’s ambitions in Korea were halted; the war drained Japanese resources and weakened Hideyoshi’s regime.
• **Political** – Strengthened Ming’s influence over Joseon; Joseon’s diplomatic ties with Ming were reinforced.
• **Cultural** – The war prompted the development of Korean naval technology (turtle ships) and the spread of firearms.
• **Economic** – Devastation of Korean agriculture and infrastructure; heavy war reparations imposed on Japan. | | **Historical Significance** | • Demonstrated the importance of naval power and innovative tactics (Yi Sun-sin’s use of “geobukseon”).
• Highlighted the vulnerability of East Asian states to external aggression and the necessity of strong alliances.
• Influenced subsequent Japanese military reforms and the eventual decline of the Toyotomi regime. | **Quick Facts** - **Duration:** 6 years (1592–1598) - **Estimated casualties:** ~1–2 million (including civilians) - **Key figures:** Yi Sun-sin (Korean admiral), Toyotomi Hideyoshi (Japanese leader), Ming generals such as Li Rusong and Chen Lin.
